articles.title: VOLUME 3 NUMBER 7 OFFICIAL PUBLICATION OF THE SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION JULY, 1992
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is progressing with the design of its new observatory at the proposed Grant Ranch site, prioritizing public service, accessibility, and future expansion. The publication also details a busy calendar of July and August 1992 events, including multiple star parties, general meetings, and beginning astronomy classes. A report from a past astronomy class covers topics such as polar precession, polar alignment, and sidereal time.

articles.title: Bill Dellinges
articles.summary: The author recounts a trip through Arizona, where he visited two dedicated amateur astronomers operating private observatories. He first describes meeting Ken Zeigler in Globe, who uses his extensive backyard facility for student photometry and personal projects. Later, in Ajo, the author connects with Bill Jorgavich, owner of Window Pane Observatory, a rental facility, and discusses Jorgavich's efforts to reduce light pollution in town.

articles.title: RTMC 1992
articles.summary: The article reviews the 24th Riverside Telescope Makers Conference (RTMC) in 1992, noting the emotional retirement of long-time organizer Cliff Holmes and the smooth transition to new leadership. It describes the vendor experience, new product displays from companies like Meade and Celestron, various workshops, and notable attendees. Despite minor issues like rain and aggressive vendor sales tactics, the event was well-attended and featured impressive amateur-built telescopes and advanced equipment.

articles.title: Beginning Astronomy Class
articles.summary: The 'Beginning Astronomy Class' focused on the Analemma, defining it as a figure-eight path illustrating the Sun's declination and equation of time, commonly found on globes. The discussion included how it relates to Earth's orbital speed variations, referencing a 1979 Sky & Telescope photograph, and concluded with a list of attendees, emphasizing the importance of public astronomy education.

articles.title: ANUAL DUES
articles.summary: Membership dues are increasing by $2 annually starting July 1st. The *Sky and Telescope* subscription rate is also increasing by $2, bringing the member rate to $20 (a $7 discount), with renewals still processed by the Treasurer. Additionally, members can now order materials directly from *Sky and Telescope* using a toll-free number to receive a 10% club discount.

articles.title: Directions to our Favorite Places
articles.summary: This article provides essential directions to three key locations for astronomy enthusiasts: the Milpitas Library for board meetings, general meetings, and beginning astronomy classes; Houge Park for public star parties; and Fremont Peak State Park for star parties and the annual summer picnic. It encourages both members and the public to attend these events, highlighting opportunities for learning, discussion, and equipment assistance.

articles.title: More Astro Ads
articles.summary: This document features classified advertisements for used astronomical equipment, including a Celestron C8 telescope, a Nagler eyepiece, and various Celestron binoculars. It also includes an important reminder about membership renewal, provides maps for a general meeting site and a public star party location, and references an ephemeris for July 1992.

articles.title: FREMONT PEAK STATE PARK
articles.summary: This document outlines features and practical information for visitors to Fremont Peak State Park, highlighting its telescope/observatory, traditional camp areas, and amenities like BBQ sites and restrooms. It provides directions, parking details (small fee, but free for residents/after-hours traffic), and encourages visitors to dress warmly for longer stays. The guide appears to be from July 1992.

articles.title: July 1992
articles.summary: This article, titled "July 1992" by Richard Stanton, serves as an astronomical guide for the month, providing detailed information on lunar phases and the rise, transit, and set times for the Moon and five nearer planets (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn). It also includes data on astronomical twilight, sidereal time, and identifies the darkest observing night, with all times specified in Pacific Daylight Time.

articles.title: PLEASE TAKE NOTE !!
articles.summary: This document serves as an urgent warning that access to Grant Ranch will be restricted after 10:00 pm, as the gates will be closed. Attempting to enter after this time is prohibited and risks tire damage due to a rollover mechanism.

articles.title: Public Star Parties
articles.summary: Paul Barton describes the joys and challenges of hosting public star parties, highlighting the enthusiasm of children learning to use telescopes and the appreciation from attendees. While some events faced issues like bad weather or low turnout, a successful party at Dilworth School showcased the positive impact of these community astronomy efforts. The author encourages others to join in coordinating and participating in these educational outreach events.

articles.title: Appologies
articles.summary: This article is an apology from Jack Zeiders regarding issues that occurred at the June General meeting at the Milpitas Library. Problems included incorrect data loaded into digital setting circles and a lack of coordination in obtaining the meeting room key. The scheduled speaker, Dr. Romani, was notified and will be rescheduled for a future event.

articles.title: Public Relation/Publicity
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is seeking a member to manage public relations and publicity efforts. This role involves promoting SJAA's events like school star parties, Houge Park activities, and astronomy classes, as well as raising awareness about other regional astronomy clubs. The volunteer would utilize existing media contacts to keep amateur astronomy in the public eye.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: Astro Ads provide a free advertising service for noncommercial entities looking to sell astronomically related products or services. Ads must be submitted to Editor Bob Madden by the 12th of each month and will run for approximately three months. This service facilitates exchanges within the astronomy community.

articles.title: Offices and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document provides a directory of key personnel, listing the names, positions, and contact phone numbers for the organization's Offices and Board of Directors. It also includes contact information for Ephemeris Contributors and the Editor, serving as a vital contact list for internal and external communication.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: This article provides updates on several comets, noting that Tanaka-Machholtz and Shoemaker-Levey are currently visible, with Tanaka-Machholtz experiencing outbursts and Shoemaker-Levey brightening. It also details the recent discoveries of Comet Spacewatch (1992h), observed at magnitude 19, and Comet Bradfield (1992l), discovered at magnitude 10 by William Bradfield, which rapidly dimmed after reaching perihelion.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document provides ephemerides for two comets, Shoemaker-Levy (1991a₁) and Tanaka-Machholz (1992d), detailing their celestial coordinates, elongation, and magnitude from late June to early August. Additionally, it includes a comprehensive classifieds section featuring various used astronomical equipment for sale, such as telescopes, mirrors, and accessories, with contact information for sellers.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association publishes a monthly bulletin called 'EPHEMERIS'. Members are encouraged to submit typed articles to editor Bob Madden by the 12th of the previous month for publication consideration.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), outlining different membership tiers including standard, junior, and one bundled with a Sky & Telescope subscription, along with their respective costs. It provides instructions for submitting the form, payment details, and contact information for the association's treasurer and general inquiries. The form facilitates joining or renewing membership for the SJAA, a non-profit organization.
